newsitem.title: URUGUAY: SOCCER-OWN GOAL GIVES URUGUAY CRUCIAL WIN OVER BOLIVIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-OWN GOAL GIVES URUGUAY CRUCIAL WIN OVER BOLIVIA.

text.p: Uruguay scored a crucial World Cup qualifying win over Bolivia, the team that denied them a trip to the 1994 finals, thanks to an own goal by defender Juan Manuel Pena on Tuesday.
The Bolivian defender inadvertently headed the ball into his own net in the 62nd minute of a nerve-wracking encounter as he attempted to clear a Uruguayan cross.
The goal was a cruel blow for Bolivia's veteran goalkeeper Carlos Trucco, who had performed heroics to keep the Uruguay attack at bay until that point.

The once mighty Uruguayans, who twice won the World Cup during the early days of the tournament, desperately needed a win after losing their last two qualifying games, one of them at home to unfancied Paraguay.
Coach Hector Nunez virtually implored veteran midfielder Enzo Francescoli, 35 next month, to come back out of international retirement to help the Uruguayan cause.

Bolivia, who qualified for the 1994 tournament in the United States at Uruguay's expense, were playing their first game under Spanish coach Antonio Lopes, brought back little more than one year after abandoning the job.

Uruguay, backed by a capacity 70,000 crowd, put the Bolivians under pressure from the start, but the lack of understanding between strikers Daniel Fonseca and Marcelo Otero plus the excellent form of Trucco prevented them from breaking down the Bolivian defence.
The home team appeared to be running out of steam until Pena's fatal error.
Bolivia had defender Sergio Castillo sent off in the 78th minute for a second bookable defence while Uruguay substitute Luis Romero had a goal disallowed five minutes from the end for offside.

Uruguay - Robert Siboldi, Guillermo Sanguinetti, Jose Herrera, Paolo Montero, Gustavo Meendez, Gabriel Cedres, Marcelo Saralegui (Alvaro Gutierrez, 81st minute), Gustavo Poyet (Luis Romero, 61st), Enzo Francescoli, Marcelo Otero (Pablo Bengoechea, 79th), Daniel Fonseca.

Bolivia - Carlos Trucco, Sergio Castillo, Marco Sandy, Juan Manuel Pena, Luis Cristaldo, Oscar Sanchez, Vladimir Soria, Ruben Tufino, 34th), Julio Baldivieso (Milton Coimbra, 69th), Milton Melgar, Jaime Moreno, Ramiro Castillo.
